title: Monotonicity testing of Boolean functions

problem.name: Monotonicity testing of Boolean functions
problem.statement_latex:
\textbf{Monotonicity testing of Boolean functions.} For $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, distinguish $x\le y\Rightarrow f(x)\le f(y)$ from distance at least $\varepsilon$ to every monotone Boolean function, using membership queries.

\textbf{Monotonicity testing from quantum examples.} Distinguish monotone Boolean functions on $\{0,1\}^n$ from functions $\varepsilon$-far from monotone using independent uniform quantum examples $2^{-n/2}\sum_x|x,f(x)\rangle$. Classical access consists of passive uniform labeled samples.
problem.statement_text: Monotonicity testing of Boolean functions. For $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, distinguish $x\le y\Rightarrow f(x)\le f(y)$ from distance at least $\varepsilon$ to every monotone Boolean function, using membership queries. Monotonicity testing from quantum examples. Distinguish monotone Boolean functions on $\{0,1\}^n$ from functions $\varepsilon$-far from monotone using independent uniform quantum examples $2^{-n/2}\sum_x|x,f(x)\rangle$. Classical access consists of passive uniform labeled samples.

quantum.headline_latex: \textbf{Monotonicity testing of Boolean functions.} $\widetilde O(n^{1/4}/\sqrt\varepsilon)$ queries by Belovs--Blais quantum monotonicity testing.
quantum.details_latex: \textbf{Monotonicity testing from quantum examples.} $\widetilde O(n^2\log(1/\delta)/\varepsilon^2)$ quantum examples by Caro--Naik--Slote, with failure probability $\delta$.
quantum.headline_text: Monotonicity testing of Boolean functions. $\widetilde O(n^{1/4}/\sqrt\varepsilon)$ queries by Belovs–Blais quantum monotonicity testing.
quantum.details_text: Monotonicity testing from quantum examples. $\widetilde O(n^2\log(1/\delta)/\varepsilon^2)$ quantum examples by Caro–Naik–Slote, with failure probability $\delta$.

classical.headline_latex: \textbf{Monotonicity testing of Boolean functions.} $\widetilde O(\sqrt n/\varepsilon^2)$ queries by the directed-isoperimetric classical tester. At constant distance, adaptive classical lower bounds are $n^{1/2-o(1)}$.
classical.details_latex: \textbf{Monotonicity testing from quantum examples.} $\exp(\Omega(\min\{\sqrt n/\varepsilon,n\}))$ passive samples are necessary in the theorem's parameter regime; learning the truth table gives an $O(n2^n)$-sample upper bound.
